Style B: the use-case documents

Island 1.1's three use cases, an input and an output each, and the two building blocks they share. Every specimen is drawn by its concept's function in world/concepts/calibration/B-docs/, in style B with the grammar of the validated document, at whole size (one pixel per unit), at 1/3 and at 1/20. No letters: titles, names, dates and text are rules, chips and pips.

The building blocks

document

A document: a rounded sheet at 108:130 lying on the paper, a title rule, full-width ruled lines. Its kind changes one small feature: plain, note (a clinic's letterhead), species (a figure plate), contract (a centred title over a double rule), judgment (a court seal, an inner border), aged (an old foxed page).


highlight

A highlight: a marker stroke over a stretch of a line, translucent, with a faint glow. Five categories, top to bottom: condition (lemon), medication (lime), allergy (signal red-pink, drawn stronger), difference (hot pink), citation (violet).


insect

An insect: a butterfly from above, wings spread as on a plate, the taxonomist's family. Parameters tell near-copies apart: two or three white spots, a tail, a bar.


The doctor: input → output

clinical_note

A clinical note: a clinic's letterhead with a cross, a patient line, three dated entries.

→

clinical_report

The same note handed back: the condition, the medication and the ALLERGY highlighted, the allergy flagged on the edge; a legend card of the three, each a chip beside its pictogram.

The taxonomist: input → output

species_description

A species description: the insect in a figure plate with a scale bar, then the description's two paragraphs.

→

matched_description

Her draft (left) and an old description (right, aged): the same insect and lines but for a third white spot and one line; both differences marked on both pages, and a link with a chain joins the figures.

The lawyer: input → output

contract

A contract: a centred title, three clause blocks numbered by pips, two signatures.

→

clause_and_judgment

The contract with its second clause highlighted, linked to the passage of a court judgment (seal, border, indented paragraphs) that rules on it.
